_comment: -p/--print: non-interactive, prints final response and exits.
--output-format text (DEV-AUTO-02.2.1): the model's own text
output only, no outer transport envelope. `--output-format json`
wraps the agent's answer inside a Claude CLI-specific envelope
object (duration_api_ms/session_id/usage/.../result/...) with the
actual workflow JSON nested as an escaped string inside the
envelope's `result` field -- WriterResult/ReviewerResult would
then parse the wrong (outer) JSON object and always see a missing
'status'/'verdict' field. text output has no such envelope; the
workflow prompt already instructs the agent to report its result
as a single JSON object on the LAST line of output (see
prompts.py), which is exactly what agent_results.py's
last-non-empty-line JSON extraction expects.
--permission-mode acceptEdits: auto-approve file edit/write tool
calls (the Writer role's whole job is CAN_EDIT_REPO within
allowed_files -- enforced separately by the orchestrator's scope
gate, not by this CLI flag).
--permission-prompts none: anything else that would need interactive
approval is auto-denied instead of hanging forever waiting for a
human who is not there (there is no human in a subprocess).
--allowedTools (DEV-AUTO-02.3): a real D0103 Writer run hit this
exact gap -- acceptEdits only auto-approves file edit/write tool
calls, NOT Bash. Without an explicit allow-list, every Bash call
(including plain `git status`/`python -m pytest ...`) requires
approval, and since --permission-prompts none auto-denies anything
needing approval, the Writer's own self-verification step (its
prompt requires it to run Targeted tests/Static checks before
reporting SUCCESS, see build_writer_prompt/_WRITER_RESULT_FORMAT
in prompts.py) was silently denied every time -- confirmed via a
real `claude -p --output-format json` smoke run whose
`permission_denials` array listed the denied Bash calls verbatim.
`Bash(<prefix> *)` syntax and matching semantics (single, non-
chained commands only -- see below) were confirmed the same way,
not guessed from --help alone. Scope is the minimum needed for
Writer's own status/diff/HEAD inspection plus running
targeted_tests/static_checks-shaped commands (python/pytest,
ruff, mypy) -- NOT a general-purpose shell allow-list.
--disallowedTools (DEV-AUTO-02.3): explicit tool-level denial of
every git-mutation subcommand, even though `Bash(git *)` is
deliberately NOT used as the allow pattern (git allow-list above
is scoped to status/diff/rev-parse only). This is defense-in-depth
on top of that scoping and on top of the Writer prompt's own
'you may not commit, push, or independently declare acceptance'
instruction (DEV-AUTO-02 Non-Fatal-If-Prompt-Ignored principle:
do not rely solely on prompt instructions for destructive
operations when a tool-level restriction is available). Confirmed
empirically that an explicit --disallowedTools entry overrides a
broader --allowedTools match for the same command (e.g. `Bash(git
reset *)` denied `git reset --hard HEAD` even under a `Bash(git
*)` allow rule in a throwaway test repo, verified via
`permission_denials` AND the file content being unchanged
afterward) -- not assumed from unwritten precedence rules.
Writer's own capability set (CAN_EDIT_REPO, CAN_RUN_TESTS -- see
model.py ROLE_CAPABILITIES) has neither CAN_COMMIT nor CAN_PUSH,
so add/commit/push/checkout/reset/clean/branch are all denied
unconditionally (Writer never legitimately needs any of them).
Compound/chained commands (`cmd1; cmd2`, `cmd1 && cmd2`) are NOT
matched by these simple prefix rules and are auto-denied as a
side effect (confirmed empirically) -- an incidental but useful
defense against using a single allowed prefix to smuggle a
second, disallowed command. Not relied upon as the primary
protection; the explicit --disallowedTools entries above are.
Prompt is appended as the trailing positional argument by
LocalCommandExecutor (prompt_via=arg), matching `claude`'s
`[options] [command] [prompt]` usage.
Separate invocation/process from the Writer, with its own reviewer
prompt (build_reviewer_prompt / build_closure_reviewer_prompt) that
explicitly instructs READ ONLY behavior.
--output-format text (DEV-AUTO-02.2.1): same reasoning as the Writer
above -- avoids Claude CLI's outer JSON transport envelope so
ReviewerResult.from_raw_output() parses the agent's own last-line
JSON verdict object, not the CLI's envelope.
--permission-mode dontAsk (DEV-AUTO-02.3, was `plan`): `plan` mode
was tried first (a read/inspect-oriented mode that does not apply
file edits) but empirically deadlocks this noninteractive setup:
with the real build_reviewer_prompt() (substantial enough to
trigger it), `plan` mode required writing an actual plan file to
~/.claude/plans/... before doing anything else, but with only
Bash in --tools (no Write) the agent could not create that file
(and creating it via Bash was itself denied as a sensitive path)
-- an approval state nobody could answer (confirmed via a real
smoke run whose result text described exactly this deadlock and
asked a human to intervene). `dontAsk` was then confirmed via the
same real smoke run (both the simple ad hoc prompt and the real
build_reviewer_prompt()) to avoid this plan-file requirement
entirely while still fully respecting --permission-prompts none
and the --allowedTools/--disallowedTools rules below (a real
`git commit -am ...` attempt was still denied and left git log
unchanged) -- read-only is enforced by --tools/--allowedTools/
--disallowedTools below, not by the permission-mode choice.
--restricted --tools Bash (DEV-AUTO-02.3): `--restricted` alone
removes Bash entirely (`ROLE_CAPABILITIES` declares
CAN_RUN_TESTS for REVIEWER in model.py, but with plain
--restricted that capability was nominal only -- the Reviewer
could not run git status/diff/pytest/ruff/mypy itself, matching
the exact gap this round fixes). Per `claude --help`,
`--restricted` removes Bash/PowerShell/REPL/etc 'unless --tools
names them' -- `--tools Bash` restores only the Bash tool while
keeping every other --restricted protection intact (ignores
user/project/local settings files, confines file tools to the
working directory, refuses bypassPermissions, gates writes to
settings/git/tool-config files to a human/permission handler).
Confirmed via a real smoke run in a throwaway git repo that this
combination lets `git rev-parse`/`git status`/`python -c` run
with zero permission_denials while Edit/Write/git mutation stay
blocked.
--allowedTools (DEV-AUTO-02.3): same narrow read-only/validation
scope as the Writer's allow-list above (git status/diff/
rev-parse, python, ruff, mypy) -- no git-mutation prefix is ever
in this list.
--disallowedTools Edit,Write,MultiEdit,NotebookEdit,git-mutation:
explicit defense-in-depth denial of every file-mutation tool AND
every git-mutation subcommand (add/commit/push/checkout/reset/
clean/branch), on top of --restricted itself
(Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit are not even in --tools, so
this is a second, redundant-by-design layer for those four), and
the orchestrator's own git-state diff comparison below. Reviewer
has no CAN_EDIT_REPO/CAN_COMMIT/CAN_PUSH capability at all (see
model.py ROLE_CAPABILITIES) -- none of these denials removes
anything the Reviewer legitimately needs.
--permission-prompts none: same non-interactive fail-closed reason
as the Writer.
-- (DEV-AUTO-02.2.1): required end-of-options marker. Any of the
variadic list flags above (--tools/--allowedTools/
--disallowedTools) would otherwise swallow the prompt string
that LocalCommandExecutor appends after this command array
(prompt_via=arg) as extra (bogus) list entries instead of reading
it as the prompt -- confirmed via a real LocalCommandExecutor
smoke run.
Compound/chained commands (`cmd1; cmd2`, `cmd1 && cmd2`) are NOT
matched by the --allowedTools prefix rules and are auto-denied as
a side effect (confirmed empirically) -- not relied upon as the
primary protection.
This CLI-level restriction is a second, independent layer on top of
the orchestrator's own pre/post git-state diff comparison in
orchestrator.py, which rejects the reviewer's verdict outright if the
repository was modified during the reviewer's execution -- so
read-only is enforced even if a future CLI flag change loosens the
options above.
